Key Takeaways Choosing an AI employee experience platform in 2026 requires looking beyond marketing claims to evaluate nine critical dimensions that determine real-world success for distributed teams. • Integration capabilities matter most : Platforms must connect seamlessly with existing HR tech stacks through native connectors or custom APIs, with SSO reducing help desk calls by 75% and proper data synchronization preventing AI hallucination from fragmented information. • Verify actual AI capabilities, not buzzwords : Look for proven predictive analytics (XGBoost achieving 0.95 AUC for retention), generative AI for personalized learning paths, and agentic automation that saves workers 97 minutes weekly on average. • Data privacy is non-negotiable : Ensure GDPR, CCPA, and HIPAA compliance with AES-256 encryption, role-based access controls, and proper legal bases for processing—GDPR fines reach €20 million or 4% of global turnover. • Calculate true total cost of ownership : Base subscriptions hide implementation fees (INR 2-8 million for enterprise platforms), AI add-ons (INR 4,219/agent/month for features like Copilot), and usage-based charges that can exceed per-employee pricing by 30-45%. • Scalability for distributed teams requires specialized features : With 72% of companies operating across multiple time zones, platforms need automated timezone detection, DST adjustment, native language translations, and support for hybrid work models. • Adoption support determines success or failure : Companies investing in cultural change and structured training achieve 5.3× higher success rates, while platforms offering free unlimited training and sub-1-hour response times drive sustained usage versus those creating workarounds. Look for platforms that support single sign-on (SSO) with protocols like SAML or OAuth, and ensure they offer real-time or near-real-time data synchronization to prevent information silos that can undermine AI accuracy. Q2. What specific AI features should I look for beyond basic automation? Focus on platforms offering predictive analytics for employee retention (using proven algorithms like XGBoost or Random Forest), generative AI for creating personalized learning paths and career development plans, AI assistants that automate repetitive workflows, and agentic automation capable of handling complex multi-step processes. Verify these capabilities with concrete performance metrics rather than accepting marketing claims at face value. Q3. The platform should demonstrate compliance with GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, and other relevant regulations depending on your operating regions. Look for AES-256 encryption for data at rest, TLS 1.3 for data in transit, role-based access controls, and multi-factor authentication. Ensure the vendor has clear breach notification procedures (GDPR requires 72-hour notification) and provides transparent privacy notices explaining how AI systems process employee information. Q4. What hidden costs should I account for when budgeting for an AI employee experience platform? Beyond base subscription fees, factor in implementation and onboarding costs (which can range from INR 2-8 million for enterprise platforms), AI feature add-ons (such as AI Copilot features that may cost INR 4,000+ per agent monthly), custom integration development, data migration expenses, and ongoing training costs. Usage-based pricing models may offer 30-45% lower total cost of ownership compared to per-employee pricing, especially if adoption rates are uncertain. Q5. How important is vendor support for successful platform adoption? Vendor support is critical—companies investing in structured training and change management achieve 5.3 times higher success rates. Look for platforms offering free unlimited training, role-based education for different user groups, self-service knowledge bases, and customer support with response times under one hour. Implementation timelines typically range from 6-8 weeks for focused deployments to 14-28 months for enterprise-wide rollouts, so ensure the vendor provides clear milestones and dedicated support throughout the process.

title: Introducing iMessage Support for Mastra Agents
summary: Let users chat to your agents using iMessage on iPhone, iPad, or Mac.
body_text: Your Mastra agents can now send and receive messages using iMessage on iPhone, iPad, or Mac. The Photon chat adapter enables direct and group chat messages and uses your agent's webhook URL to handle two-way communication. iMessage conversations have a limited surface area available to help you debug or monitor agent behavior. Mastra's observability system provides visibility into each trace, letting you inspect and debug each run. Your browser does not support the video tag. Agent interactions differ from app to app. Some conversations are more suited to mobile chat interfaces, others to desktop applications. Choosing the most suitable interface can enhance user experience. iMessage joins Mastra's existing channel adapters: Slack , Discord , WhatsApp , Microsoft Teams , and more, letting you choose the right UI for your users. Delivery reliability varies by channel. Photon retries failed messages so duplicate deliveries can occasionally occur. Mastra automatically dedupes using in-memory keys, which persist in long-running instances but can be lost in serverless environments. To persist dedupe keys across cold starts, restarts, or crashes, add createRedisState() to your agent's channels.state . Get started Install the iMessage adapter: Terminal npm install @photon-ai/chat-adapter-imessage note Requires @mastra/core@1.56.0 or later, added in PR #20702 . Add createiMessageAdapter() to your agent's channels.adapters object: src/mastra/agents/concierge-agent.ts import { Agent } from " @mastra/core/agent " ; import { createiMessageAdapter } from " @photon-ai/chat-adapter-imessage " ; export const conciergeAgent = new Agent ({ id: " concierge-agent " , name: " Concierge Agent " , description: " Handles restaurant bookings over iMessage " , instructions: /* ... */ , model: " anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 " , channels: { adapters: { imessage: { adapter: createiMessageAdapter (), toolDisplay: " hidden " , gateway: false } } } }); toolDisplay: "hidden" — hides tool call details from message output gateway: false — disables the gateway listener when using webhooks For more information and full configuration options, see: iMessage Channels overview

title: Urban One to Launch “ONE Yard: The HBCU Experience”—a Multi-City Tour Bringing the Cultural Power of the HBCU Yard to Life
summary: Our mission is to be the most trusted source in the African-American community that informs, entertains and inspires our audience by providing culturally relevant integrated content through our radio, television, and digital platforms.
body_text: Urban One to Launch “ONE Yard: The HBCU Experience”—a Multi-City Tour Bringing the Cultural Power of the HBCU Yard to Life Press Room , Urban One In The News 0 As Gen Z battles “algorithm fatigue,” the media powerhouse expands its HBCU commitment—giving brands a direct bridge to 80 million consumers and the 90% of Black audiences who back companies that invest in HBCUs SILVER SPRING, MD, August 11, 2026 — Urban One , the nation’s largest distributor of Black and Urban content, today announced the official launch of ONE Yard: The HBCU Experience , a multi-city engagement tour celebrating the culture, community, and legacy of Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). Originally born as a digital sanctuary, ONE Yard is stepping outside of the screen and hitting the ground to deliver immersive, live on-campus experiences at Bowie State University on August 27 and Clark Atlanta University on September 2. Today’s younger audiences are experiencing “algorithm fatigue” and actively seeking genuine, physical spaces rooted in community and shared joy. Urban One is answering this call by honoring the HBCU yard as the epicenter for gathering. Designed as a vibrant village of culture, entertainment, wellness, and career empowerment, each stop will feature celebrity hosts, top Black influencers and digital creators, live DJs, notable alumni, and special guests. “For decades, Urban One has been an anchor in the HBCU community. With ONE Yard , we’re creating a powerful, scalable gateway for brands looking to engage meaningfully with Gen Z. By combining live on-the-ground activations with digital storytelling, we are providing our partners with an unmatched opportunity to drive culture and connect with this generation on an entirely new level,” said Jeff Meza, Urban One’s EVP, Head of Branded Entertainment & Integrated Marketing . ONE Yard ’s signature on-the-ground activations include: Aura Arcade: Hosted by PlayVS, this arcade-style gaming hub allows students to compete, connect, and put their joystick skills on full display. 3rd Space by Live Wire: A reimagined main stage with curated programming, performances, and a special HBCU edition taping of Live Wire for HipHopWired.com. Wellness Zone: A dedicated wellness, beauty, and grooming oasis featuring personalized skin insights, yoga, meditation, and an affirmation station. Cookout Corridor: A tailgate-themed food and beverage zone where guests can refuel and experience regional local cuisine and signature flavors. Your University Row: A one-stop resource hub with the professional guidance, career tools, and entrepreneurial support needed to navigate life beyond graduation. The Promenade: A photo moment where guests step inside a life-size Cassius magazine cover for a shareable, social-ready experience celebrating HBCU style. “ ONE Yard gives brands the opportunity to do more than show up on campus—it enables them to invest meaningfully in the culture, talent and future of HBCU communities. By combining Urban One’s cultural intelligence and first-party data with our trusted media brands, creators and live experiences, we help partners connect with the culture makers shaping what’s next, create new opportunities for commerce and deliver measurable business impact,” shared Tiffany Nasralla, Urban One’s Co-Chief Revenue Officer . ONE Yard is part of Urban One’s long-term investment in emerging HBCU voices. Built in close partnership with local HBCU leaders and student organizations, every activation is designed to boost student success and retention. Through hands-on portfolio building, industry mentorship, and clear career pathways, ONE Yard bridges the gap between campus life and professional success. For more information about ONE Yard: The HBCU Experience and for students to register, please visit, www.oneyard.co . About Urban One, Inc. Urban One, Inc. ( urban1.com ) is the largest diversified media company primarily targeting Black Americans and Urban consumers in the U.S., reaching 80 million unique consumers monthly. Its assets include TV One and CLEO TV, collectively available in 38 million households, with CTV generating 135 million monthly impressions; Radio One, with 74 broadcast stations in 13 top African American markets; and REACH Media, with 311 affiliates over 93 markets and home to nationally syndicated shows such as The Rickey Smiley Morning Show, The D.L. Hughley Show, Get Up! Mornings with Erica Campbell and The Morning Hustle. Urban One’s digital division, iONE Digital, boasts 300 million monthly videos views, and engages 31 million monthly readers across leading brands like Bossip, HipHopWired, MadameNoire, and NewsOne. ###

title: Canopy sees growing revenue, declining losses in Q1 2027

body_text: Canopy sees growing revenue, declining losses in Q1 2027 August 10, 2026 Media Outlet: STRATCANN Canopy sees growing revenue, declining losses in Q1 2027 August 7, 2026 By: Sarah Clark Canopy Growth reported net revenue of $81.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY2027), gross margin of $22.2 million, and a net loss of $14.6 million. This represented a 13% year-over-year increase compared to Q1 FY2026, and a 68% decrease in losses. Net revenue from cannabis sales was $65.1 million, up 14% YOY, with another $16.1 million from its control of Storz & Bickel, up 6% YOY. Net revenue from Canadian adult-use cannabis was up 10% YOY to $29.7 million, Canadian medical cannabis was up 22% YOY to $25.8 million, and sales into the international market were up 10% to $9.6 million. The increase in Canadian adult-use sales was primarily attributable to increased flower sales, driven by the acquisition of MTL in March 2026, partially offset by declines in opportunistic bulk sales. The year-over-year increase in Canadian medical cannabis sales was primarily attributed to continued growth in the number of insured customers and the acquisition of MTL, partially offset by the Canadian government’s Veterans Affairs Canada reduction in the reimbursement rate paid to producers for medical cannabis from $8.50 a gram to $6 a gram, which became effective on April 1, 2026. The year-over-year increase in international sales was primarily attributed to strength in Europe, specifically in Poland. The year-over-year increase in Storz & Bickel was attributed to prior-year product portfolio expansion and growth in non-core markets. Cost of Canopy’s goods sold increased 9% while gross margin increased by 23%. Canopy incurred $16.2 million in excise taxes on its Canadian non-medical sales (35% of gross sales), and $3 million on its Canadian medical cannabis sales (10% of gross sales), for a total of $19.2 million (25% total). Total net sales in Canada were $54.9 million, a 14% YOY increase, while sales in the German market were another $17.6 million (22% increase YOY), sales into the US market were $6.2 million (a 43% increase YOY), and other markets combined were another $2.4 million (a 32% decline YOY). “The renewed focus and strong momentum we established over the past year have continued into fiscal 2027,” said Luc Mongeau, Chief Executive Officer. “In the first quarter, we achieved net revenue growth in every business through solid execution across the organization. We have clear strategies to deliver further growth in each of our end markets. At the heart of our cannabis strategy is our company-wide push to elevate cultivation and produce a consistent and increasing supply of high-quality flower that will support growing demand both in Canada and internationally.” Download PDF June 16, 2026 Medical cannabis: the driving force behind Canopy Growth’s recovery Media By Aurélien BERNARD Canadian cannabis producer Canopy Growth announced a significant improvement in its financial results for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, driven by strong growth in both the medical cannabis sector and its international operations. These results suggest that the restructuring efforts the company has been undertaking for several years may finally be starting to pay off. title: Best IB Subject Combinations for Medicine
summary: Best IB subjects for medicine, explained for parents: compare HL combinations, protect university options, and plan effectively for strong IB exam results.
body_text: Choosing IB subjects can feel uncomfortably permanent. A parent sees six boxes on a form; a student sees two years of lessons, assessments, and examinations. Somewhere beyond both sits a medical school admissions page with requirements that may change by country and university. The reassuring answer is straightforward: for the widest access to undergraduate medicine, the safest combination is Biology HL and Chemistry HL, followed by a third HL subject in which the student can earn a strong grade . Mathematics, Physics, Psychology, and a language can all work as the third HL, depending on university requirements and the student's strengths. This is not a universal rule. Oxford currently requires Chemistry HL plus at least one of Biology, Physics, or Mathematics at HL, while institutions such as UCL require both Biology and Chemistry at HL. Australian prerequisites vary considerably, and medicine in the United States is normally entered after an undergraduate degree. The right decision therefore begins with a shortlist, not with assumptions. An IB student and parent consulting a suspicious subject-selection machine The short answer for parents Use this checklist before confirming any IB HL and SL subjects: Put Biology and Chemistry at HL if the goal is to preserve the broadest range of direct-entry medicine options. Select the third HL according to both admissions requirements and genuine academic strength. Check at least five likely medical programs across the countries being considered. Record required subjects, required levels, minimum HL grades, total IB scores, and any mathematics or English conditions. Avoid choosing four HL subjects merely because the combination appears more impressive. Recheck every requirement on the university's official admissions page before applying. Parents who want a broader framework may also find this guide to discussing IB subject choices and careers helpful. The goal is not to dictate a combination. It is to ensure that the student understands which choices open doors and which may quietly close them. Why Biology HL and Chemistry HL are usually safest Medicine is not one admission system. It is hundreds of institutions making slightly different decisions about academic preparation. Chemistry HL is especially important for UK applicants. Some universities pair it with Biology, while others accept another laboratory science or Mathematics. Biology HL remains the prudent companion because several competitive programs explicitly require both sciences at Higher Level. This combination also gives students relevant preparation. Biology develops understanding of systems, cellular processes, genetics, physiology, and experimental interpretation. Chemistry builds quantitative reasoning and an understanding of structure, reactions, equilibrium, energetics, and measurement. Neither guarantees admission, but together they satisfy more prerequisite patterns than most alternatives. Students debating the second science can explore the practical differences between IB Chemistry and Physics for medicine . Physics can be valuable and is accepted by some universities, but it does not replace Biology everywhere. Strong medicine subject combinations compared HL combination Best suited to Important consideration Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics Students strong in quantitative work who want broad scientific preparation Mathematics HL adds a substantial workload and is not universally required for medicine Biology, Chemistry, Psychology Students interested in behaviour and confident in essay-based evaluation Psychology is an IB Group 3 subject and normally does not replace a required laboratory science Biology, Chemistry, Language or Humanities Students whose strongest third subject is writing-based A high third-HL grade may be more useful than unnecessary scientific overload Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics Applicants targeting universities that explicitly accept this combination It can exclude programs that require Biology HL Biology, Chemistry, Physics Exceptionally strong science students with a clear reason for three sciences Availability and diploma arrangements depend on the school, and the workload can be severe Biology, Chemistry, and Mathematics HL This is often treated as the default high-achieving combination. It is rigorous, coherent, and suitable for students who genuinely enjoy mathematical problem-solving. But rigor is useful only when it produces sustainable performance. Most medical programs do not automatically prefer Mathematics HL over a different third HL. If Mathematics HL is likely to absorb time needed for Chemistry, Biology, the Extended Essay, or admissions preparation, it may weaken rather than strengthen the overall profile. The choice between mathematics courses also requires institution-level checking. Oxford currently states that it has no preference between Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation when Mathematics HL is used to meet its medicine requirements. That does not establish a rule for every university. RevisionDojo's guide to the best IB Mathematics route for medicine can help families frame the decision. Biology, Chemistry, and Psychology HL Psychology can complement medicine through research methods, critical evaluation, and the study of behaviour. It may also suit a student whose strengths extend beyond calculation-heavy subjects. However, it should be viewed as the third HL rather than a substitute for a required science. The distinction matters because IB Psychology belongs to Group 3, not Group 4. Families considering it can read whether IB Psychology suits aspiring medical students . Biology, Chemistry, and a strong language or humanity A future doctor does not need every HL to look clinical. Medicine requires comprehension, communication, structured argument, and judgement under uncertainty. A language, History, English, or another humanity may therefore be a sensible third choice when it aligns with the student's abilities. The strategic principle is simple: meet the non-negotiable science prerequisites, then protect the likelihood of excellent overall results. A balanced combination is not a less ambitious one. A student discovers that maximum difficulty is not always the best route How HL and SL choices affect medicine applications The IB normally involves six subjects, with at least three and no more than four studied at Higher Level. According to the IB, an HL course represents 240 recommended teaching hours, compared with 150 at SL. That difference explains why changing one subject level can reshape a student's entire week. For medicine, universities may specify not only the subjects but also their levels and grades. An excellent total score does not normally compensate for missing a compulsory HL prerequisite. Conversely, once the required sciences are present, adding another difficult HL does not necessarily create an admissions advantage. A sensible pattern is therefore: HL: Biology, Chemistry, and the student's strongest suitable third subject. SL: Mathematics, languages, and humanities selected to satisfy the diploma and any university-specific conditions. This is a starting framework rather than a prescription. Families uncertain about the distinction can review how universities evaluate HL and SL subjects and the practical guide to choosing IB HL subjects wisely . Country matters more than many families expect United Kingdom and other direct-entry systems UK medicine programs often publish precise IB conditions. Current examples show why checking individual universities is essential: Oxford requires Chemistry HL and another approved science or Mathematics at HL, whereas UCL specifies Biology and Chemistry at HL. Requirements may also include minimum total points, particular HL grades, English or Mathematics conditions, an admissions test, and an interview. Requirements elsewhere in Europe and Asia vary by institution, applicant status, and language of instruction. Do not apply a UK combination automatically to another country. Australia Australian medical pathways are diverse. Some direct-entry courses specify Chemistry or Mathematics, while others focus more heavily on academic rank, an admissions test, and an interview. Certain programs recommend Biology without making it a formal prerequisite. Applicants should also distinguish direct-entry, provisional-entry, and graduate-entry routes before comparing requirements. United States and Canada In the United States, students typically complete an undergraduate degree before medical school. The Association of American Medical Colleges notes that prerequisite coursework varies, although biology, English, and chemistry commonly appear. IB Biology and Chemistry can provide useful preparation, but high-school subject selection is not equivalent to completing university premedical requirements. Canadian pathways also vary and generally require university study first. Families considering North America should choose an IB combination that supports admission to an appropriate undergraduate course without assuming that it provides direct medical entry. Common subject-selection mistakes The first mistake is searching for one globally perfect combination. There is none. The best IB subjects for medicine depend on where the student may apply. The second is treating difficulty as a signal of commitment. Three demanding sciences or four HLs may sound formidable, but universities primarily need evidence that published requirements have been met. An overloaded student still has to manage internal assessments, TOK, the Extended Essay, CAS, examinations, and potentially admissions testing. The third is overlooking SL conditions. A medical program may specify acceptable Mathematics, English, or language qualifications even when those subjects are not central to the degree. The fourth is checking requirements once and assuming they will remain unchanged. Admissions rules can change between subject selection and application. Keep a dated spreadsheet and revisit official course pages before each major decision. Turn the right combination into strong results Subject selection protects eligibility. Preparation turns that eligibility into a competitive application. Once Biology HL and Chemistry HL are chosen, students should build a repeatable cycle: learn a concept, retrieve it without notes, answer exam-style questions, examine errors, and revisit weak areas under time pressure. Reading alone can create familiarity without reliable recall. A revision robot politely exposes the limits of rereading notes RevisionDojo is designed as the ultimate IB resource for that cycle. Students can move from syllabus-aligned IB Biology HL resources and IB Chemistry HL resources into Study Notes, Flashcards, and the Questionbank. AI Chat can clarify a difficult idea, while Grading tools provide feedback on written work. Predicted Papers and Mock Exams develop timing, and the Coursework Library and Tutors support longer-term work when independent study is not enough. The combination matters, but the daily system matters more than it first appears. A subject on an application form is only a promise. Consistent practice is how the student eventually keeps it. A calm final decision For most students pursuing direct-entry medicine, Biology HL and Chemistry HL are the safest foundation . The third HL should meet any remaining university requirements while giving the student a realistic opportunity to earn an excellent grade. Before confirming the subjects, build a university shortlist, verify every prerequisite on official admissions pages, and discuss the workload honestly with the school. Then stop searching for a combination that looks perfect to everyone. Choose the one that keeps the right doors open and gives the student enough capacity to walk through them. The natural next step is not another round of speculation. It is to review the current IB syllabus and subject resources , confirm the pathway, and begin building mastery in Biology and Chemistry one topic at a time.

title: SAT Study Schedule 2026: 1, 3, and 6-Month Guide
summary: Build a proven SAT Study Schedule: take a diagnostic, set goals, block weekly sessions, and follow 1-, 3-, or 6‑month timelines. Get a free template.
body_text: SAT Study Schedule 2026: 1, 3, and 6-Month Guide TL;DR An SAT study schedule maps every prep activity (diagnostics, content review, practice tests, and error analysis) to specific days and times across a set timeline. College Board data shows that just 20 hours of structured practice is associated with a 115-point score gain. The best schedules start with a diagnostic test, calculate the hours needed to close your score gap, and cycle between content work, timed exams, and mistake review. Whether you have six months or one month, a concrete schedule beats studying “whenever you feel like it” every time. Quick Answer The best SAT study schedule depends on how much your current score differs from your goal score. - 6 months: Best for beginners or students aiming to improve by 200+ points (3–5 hours per week). - 3 months: Ideal for most students seeking a 100–200 point increase (5–8 hours per week). - 1 month: Best for experienced test takers or retakes needing under 100 points (8–12 hours per week). Every effective schedule follows the same pattern: 1. Take a diagnostic test. 2. Set a target score. 3. Calculate total study hours. 4. Schedule consistent weekly sessions. 5. Alternate between learning, practice tests, and error review. 6. Reduce workload during the final days before the exam. The most important predictor of improvement is not total study time—it is consistently reviewing mistakes after every practice session. Goal Recommended Timeline Weekly Hours Practice Tests Improve 50 points 1 month 5–6 hrs Weekly Improve 100 points 2–3 months 5–8 hrs Every 2 weeks Improve 150 points 3–4 months 6–9 hrs Every 2 weeks Improve 200+ points 6 months 3–5 hrs Every 3 weeks What Is an SAT Study Schedule? An SAT study schedule is a detailed calendar that specifies when and what you will study over a defined period of time. It assigns each prep activity, from your first diagnostic test through your final review session, to specific days and time blocks across weeks or months. Think of it as the execution layer of your preparation. It answers the question most students struggle with: “What should I be doing today?” A quick distinction worth making. A study plan defines what you need to learn: your content gaps, target skills, and priority areas. A study schedule defines when you will do each of those things. The plan is strategy. The schedule is logistics. You need both, but the schedule is what keeps you accountable day to day. The shift to the Digital SAT makes scheduling even more important. The test now runs 2 hours and 14 minutes with 98 questions across two adaptive modules per section. Because each module adjusts difficulty based on your first-module performance, your schedule should include pacing drills, not just content review. Rushing through Module 1 can lower Module 2’s difficulty ceiling and cap your score. Start with a free diagnostic to find out where you stand before building your schedule. Who This SAT Study Schedule Is For This guide is designed for: First-time SAT test takers Students retaking the SAT High school sophomores and juniors planning ahead Seniors preparing for their final SAT attempt Students balancing school, sports, jobs, and extracurricular activities Homeschooled students creating independent study plans If you fall into any of these groups, choosing the correct study timeline can significantly improve your chances of reaching your target score. Why You Need an SAT Study Schedule A growing number of selective colleges have reinstated standardized test requirements, including MIT, Harvard, Yale, Stanford, Brown, Dartmouth, Cornell, Caltech, and the University of Texas at Austin. For the Class of 2025, over two million students took the SAT, with a mean total score of 1029 . A score of 1350 or above puts you in roughly the top 10% of test takers. These numbers make structured prep more consequential than it has been in years. The data on structured study time is clear. According to College Board research , just 6 to 8 hours of study with Official SAT Practice is associated with a 90-point score increase. Twenty hours is associated with a 115-point gain. And more than 16,000 students from the class of 2017 who used Official SAT Practice on Khan Academy improved their scores by over 200 points. But here is the part that matters most: the main factor is not how much time you study. It is how well you spend that time. Practitioners on Reddit and tutor blogs consistently repeat this point. A smart 3-to-6-month schedule beats a frantic cram session every time. Studying without structure leads to the three biggest mistakes students make: covering material they already know, skipping error review, and cramming the final week. A schedule prevents all three. Key Components of Every SAT Study Schedule Every effective SAT study schedule contains the same core building blocks, regardless of whether you have six months or six weeks. 1. Start with a Diagnostic Test You cannot build a targeted schedule without knowing your starting point. Skip the diagnostic and you are guessing at what to study. Take one and you turn “study everything” into “fix these two or three specific things.” This is not just tutor advice. It is near-universal consensus across r/Sat, College Board’s own guidance, and every prep company that ranks for this topic. The first entry on your schedule should always be a cold, timed diagnostic. 2. Set a Goal Score Look up the 25th-to-75th percentile SAT ranges for your target schools. Your goal score should sit at or above the 50th percentile for your most competitive school. This gives you a concrete number to work toward rather than a vague ambition to “do well.” A score predictor can help you estimate where you will land based on your current performance and study trajectory. 3. Calculate the Hours You Need Work backward from the gap between your diagnostic score and your goal score. Historical data gives us useful benchmarks: Score Improvement Needed Estimated Study Hours 0 to 50 points 10 to 20 hours 50 to 100 points 40 to 60 hours 100 to 200 points 80 to 120 hours 200+ points 150+ hours Sources: ScoreSmart, PrepScholar (which recommends about 80 hours for a 200-point gain) Once you have your total hours, divide by the number of weeks until test day. That gives you your weekly study commitment. 4. Block Your Weekly Sessions Many students say they will “study 5 hours a week” but never specify when. That is not a schedule. It is a hope. Pick your days and times in advance. If you commit to Tuesday and Thursday evenings plus Saturday morning, treat those slots with the same seriousness as a class or a job. Research on session length suggests that sessions under 30 minutes rarely build depth, while sessions over two hours often lead to fatigue and careless errors. The sweet spot for most students is 45 to 90 minutes per session. 5. Cycle Between Three Activity Types Your schedule should rotate among three kinds of work: Content days. Targeted skill work on your weakest areas. If your diagnostic shows you are losing points on algebra and evidence-based reading, those topics get the most calendar space. Drill SAT problem sets that isolate the specific skills you need. Practice test days. Full-length, timed exams taken under realistic conditions. College Board recommends spacing these out by at least two weeks when your schedule allows. Most students benefit from four to six total full-length exams across their entire prep period. Review days. This is the activity that separates students who improve from students who plateau. Go through every wrong answer. Write down what you missed and why. Keep an error log (even a simple spreadsheet works). Practitioners on Reddit are emphatic about this: multiple threads on r/Sat highlight that error analysis is where the real improvement happens, not just taking more tests. 6. Taper Before Test Day Reduce your study hours slightly in the last two to three days before the SAT. New practice tests will not create new skills in 48 hours, but they can create stress. Light review, early sleep, and a calm morning are worth more than a last-minute cram session. How Many Total Hours Should You Study for the SAT? The number of hours you need depends primarily on your target score increase. Score Increase Suggested Hours 0–50 points 10–20 50–100 points 40–60 100–200 points 80–120 200+ points 150+ These estimates assume consistent practice with official SAT materials and regular error review. Students who skip reviewing mistakes often require significantly more study time to reach the same score improvement. SAT Study Schedule by Timeline Not every student has the same amount of time. Here is what each common timeline looks like and who it works best for. Timeline Best For Weekly Hours Practice Tests 6 months Students starting from scratch or targeting a 200+ point gain 3 to 5 hours 1 every 3 weeks 3 months Most common timeline; students with a baseline who need 100 to 200 points 5 to 8 hours 1 every 2 weeks 1 month Retakers or students needing fewer than 100 points of improvement 8 to 12 hours 1 per week 2 weeks Final polish only; not recommended for first-time takers 10 to 15 hours 1 to 2 total The one-month plan deserves a warning. It is best suited for students who have already taken the SAT and need a focused refresh. If you have never taken the test, one month is almost certainly not enough to build and retain skills. Knowledge gained through cramming is shallow and fragile, and it tends to collapse under the fatigue and stress of test day. One more timing detail that catches students off guard: booking your next test date four weeks after your first sitting often feels productive, but it is usually a mistake. You will not have your first score back for about two weeks, leaving only two weeks to actually study based on what you got wrong. Tutors and prep advisors generally recommend an 8-to-12-week gap between sittings. Take a free practice exam to establish your baseline before choosing a timeline. Sample Weekly SAT Study Schedule A weekly schedule provides enough structure while leaving flexibility for school and extracurricular activities. Day Focus Time Monday SAT Math Review 60 min Tuesday Reading & Writing 60 min Wednesday Rest or Vocabulary 30 min Thursday Mixed Practice Questions 75 min Friday Error Log Review 45 min Saturday Full-Length Practice Test 2 hr 14 min Sunday Practice Test Review 90 min Repeating a predictable weekly routine helps students build study habits and reduces procrastination. How Often Should You Take Practice Tests? Practice tests are the backbone of SAT prep, but more is not always better. College Board’s recommendation is to space full-length tests by at least two weeks. Most test prep experts suggest four to six total exams across your entire preparation, typically every two to three weeks. Weekly practice tests can work during the final three or four weeks if you already have solid content knowledge, but they are counterproductive earlier in your prep when you are still learning foundational skills. Here is the rule that should govern your practice test cadence: do not take another practice test until you have thoroughly reviewed the last one. Call it the “review gate.” Every wrong answer on a practice test is a data point about what you need to study. If you skip the review and jump straight into another test, you are just collecting data you will never use. Students on r/Sat report this as one of the most common failure modes: “I took a bunch of practice tests but never reviewed them.” The students who report the biggest gains almost always mention detailed error analysis as the thing that actually moved their scores. For daily practice between full tests, targeted SAT practice questions focused on your weak areas are more productive than another timed exam. How to Stay Consistent With Your SAT Study Schedule Many students struggle not because the material is difficult, but because they stop following their schedule. Strategies that improve consistency include: Study at the same time every week. Turn off phone notifications during sessions. Track completed study hours. Review your error log every weekend. Set small weekly score goals. Reward yourself after completing major milestones. Consistency beats intensity. Four productive one-hour sessions each week are generally more effective than one six-hour cram session. Common SAT Study Schedule Mistakes Studying Without a Diagnostic First This wastes time on areas where you are already strong. The students on r/Sat who report the biggest improvements consistently describe the same approach: take a diagnostic cold, identify two or three weak areas, and drill them ruthlessly rather than trying to cover everything equally. Only Taking Practice Tests, Never Reviewing Them Practice tests without error review is like going to the doctor for bloodwork and never reading the results. The test tells you what is wrong. The review is the treatment. Cramming in the Final Week A common instinct, and almost always counterproductive. The last few days before the SAT should be light review, not new material. You are better off sleeping well and arriving calm than squeezing in one more practice test at midnight. Focusing Only on Strong Areas It feels good to practice things you are already good at. It does not raise your score. The points are hiding in your weak sections. If you hate reading comprehension, that is probably where your biggest gains live. Studying Only When Motivated Motivation is unreliable. A schedule is not. Students who study only when they feel like it end up with inconsistent preparation and uneven coverage. The whole point of a schedule is to remove the decision about whether to study today. The answer is always yes, because it is on the calendar. Tools That Help You Build and Follow an SAT Study Schedule You do not need expensive software to build a study schedule. A Google Calendar and a spreadsheet for error logging will get you far. But some tools make the process faster and more personalized. Official Bluebook app (free). College Board’s own practice platform. It simulates the actual Digital SAT interface and provides full-length practice tests. Essential for getting comfortable with the adaptive format. Khan Academy (free). Personalized practice recommendations based on your performance. The College Board partnership makes it a natural complement to Bluebook. AI-powered platforms. Tools that generate adaptive study paths based on your diagnostic results can save significant planning time. They adjust as you improve, keeping your schedule focused on whatever needs the most attention. Browse SAT resources for options that include diagnostics, AI tutoring, and progress tracking in one place. Error log template. A simple spreadsheet with columns for date, question type, what you got wrong, and why. Review it weekly. This is the single most underused tool in SAT prep. Frequently Asked Questions How many hours a week should I study for the SAT? It depends on your score gap and timeline. Students aiming for a 100-to-200-point improvement over three months typically need 5 to 8 hours per week. Those with a smaller gap or longer timeline can get by with 3 to 5 hours. The key is consistency: four sessions of 75 minutes will do more than one eight-hour marathon. Is a one-month SAT study schedule enough? For retakers who already have a solid foundation and need fewer than 100 points of improvement, yes. For first-time test takers or anyone targeting a large score gain, one month is not enough. You will not have time to learn, practice, and retain new skills before they erode under test-day pressure. Should I study before taking a diagnostic test? No. The entire purpose of a diagnostic is to reveal your actual starting point. Studying beforehand defeats that purpose. Take it cold, accept whatever score you get, and use it to build a schedule that targets your real weaknesses. How do I adjust my schedule if I am not improving? First, check whether you are actually reviewing your mistakes or just taking more tests. If your error log shows the same question types appearing repeatedly, you need to change how you are studying those topics, not just how much. Consider switching resources, trying a different explanation style, or focusing on fewer skills at a time. If you have been self-studying for several weeks without progress, outside feedback from a tutor or AI tutor can help identify blind spots. How do I fit SAT prep around school, sports, and extracurriculars? Block your study sessions at times that are already open and repeatable. Many students use weekday evenings (45 to 60 minutes) and a longer weekend session (90 minutes to 2 hours). Protect those blocks the way you would protect practice or rehearsal. The total hours matter less than the consistency. What should I study first: Math or Reading and Writing? Start with whichever section has the bigger gap between your current performance and your goal. If both are equally weak, many tutors recommend beginning with Math because the concepts are more concrete and progress tends to be more immediately visible, which builds confidence. When should I start my SAT study schedule? Three months before your test date is the most common and effective starting point for most students. Six months gives even more breathing room if you are starting from scratch. Starting earlier means lower weekly time commitments and less stress. Building a study schedule is the single most practical thing you can do to turn SAT prep from an overwhelming project into a manageable routine. The formula is straightforward: diagnostic first, goal score second, hours calculated third, sessions blocked fourth, and consistent review throughout. Start learning with a free diagnostic and personalized study path to put your schedule into action today.

Lead Enrichment From Surface
summary: Surface enriches leads as they fill out the form, not after. By the time a prospect submits, their record already carries 15 to 20 enriched data points.
body_text: Surface enriches leads as they fill out the form, not after. By the time a prospect submits, their record already carries 15 to 20 enriched data points. The Problem A prospect submits your form. Their lead record hits the CRM with a name, email, and whatever fields they bothered to fill out. Then your team has to enrich the record manually or wait for a third party tool to process it in batches. That delay matters. Reps can't prioritize leads they know nothing about. Routing rules can't fire without company data. And every hour between submission and enrichment is time your team spends working with incomplete information. Most enrichment happens after the form, disconnected from the capture process. The form collects, a separate tool enriches, and the CRM eventually gets a complete record. Surface collapses that into a single step. How Real Time Enrichment Works in Surface The moment a prospect enters their email address, Surface validates the domain and starts appending company data: employee count, industry classification, estimated revenue, headquarters location, and technology stack. This happens in milliseconds while the prospect is still on the form. Every field that gets filled triggers additional data capture in the background. Contact level data gets appended the same way. Job title, seniority level, department, and LinkedIn profile URL when available. If a prospect provides a phone number, Surface validates it and appends geographic location. What Gets Enriched Category Data points Company Employee count, industry, estimated revenue, HQ location, technology stack Contact Job title, seniority level, department, LinkedIn profile URL Validation Email domain verification, phone number validation, geographic location By the time the prospect clicks submit, their lead record already carries 15 to 20 enriched data points. Company information, contact details, and validation data are all attached before the lead ever leaves the form. Why This Matters Enrichment before submission changes what your team can do with every lead. Routing rules can use company size and industry to assign the right rep in real time. Lead scoring can factor in seniority and tech stack before the record hits the CRM. Reps see a full profile on the first notification, not a name and email they need to research. The difference is that enrichment stops being a separate step in your pipeline. It happens during capture, so everything downstream operates on complete data from the start. Frequently Asked Questions What is real time lead enrichment? Real time lead enrichment is the process of appending company and contact data to a lead record as the prospect fills out a form, not after submission. It eliminates the delay between capture and enrichment. What data does Surface enrich? Surface appends employee count, industry, revenue, HQ location, technology stack, job title, seniority level, department, LinkedIn profile URL, and validated phone number with geographic location. Does enrichment slow down the form? No. Enrichment runs in milliseconds in the background. The prospect experiences no delay or change in the form. When does enrichment start? The moment a prospect enters their email address. Surface validates the domain and begins appending company data immediately while the prospect continues filling out the form. Does enriched data sync to my CRM? Yes. All enriched data points are attached to the lead record and sync to your CRM alongside the form submission. No separate enrichment tool needed.

title: Greg Luhman discusses how AI can act as a force multiplier for broadband providers at Core Tel Forum 2026
summary: Session will examine how emerging AI tools help service providers work more efficiently, answer complex questions and improve broadband network operations
body_text: Speakers: Greg Luhman, business development manager at Adtran Topics: AI and your broadband network When: Thursday, August 20, 10:10 a.m. CDT Where: Core Tel Forum 2026, Brainerd, Minnesota, USA https://www.coretelecom.net/tel-forums Artificial intelligence is rapidly moving from experimentation to everyday use, influencing how people work, learn and make decisions. (“IES”) (NASDAQ: IESC) today announced that it has entered into a definitive
body_text: IES Holdings to Acquire DBM Global Aug 10, 2026 at 8:00 AM EDT PDF Version Transaction Establishes New Structural Line of Business, Adding One of the Largest Independent Structural Steel Fabrication and Erection Platforms in the U.S. HOUSTON, Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- IES Holdings, Inc. (“IES”) (NASDAQ: IESC) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire DBM Global Inc. (“DBM Global”), a vertically integrated structural steel fabrication, erection and industrial services platform, from INNOVATE Corp. (“INNOVATE”) (NYSE: VATE) (the “Transaction”). The consideration for DBM Global, including minority interests, is approximately $650 million, comprised of cash and shares of IES common stock. IES expects to fund the cash portion of the consideration through a combination of cash on hand and borrowings under an expanded credit facility being arranged by Wells Fargo. DBM Global generated revenue of approximately $1.3 billion for the twelve months ended March 31, 2026. DBM Global, headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, employs approximately 3,400 people and operates through a family of established brands, including Schuff Steel, Banker Steel, GrayWolf, DBM Vircon and Aitken, providing engineering, fabrication, erection and industrial construction services across commercial, industrial, data center, stadium and infrastructure end markets. DBM Global's platform includes over 2 million square feet of fabrication and operating facilities across the United States and has provided structural steel and erection services to many of the country's most recognizable projects. Upon closing of the Transaction, DBM Global will operate as a new Structural line of business for IES, further diversifying IES's operations alongside its existing Communications, Residential, Infrastructure Solutions, and Commercial & Industrial segments. The Transaction is expected to close in the quarter ending December 31, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals and other conditions set forth in the definitive agreement, with the final consideration subject to customary net working capital and other true-up adjustments. Strategic Rationale Scaled national platform: DBM Global is one of the largest independent structural steel fabrication and erection platforms in the U.S., with a coast-to-coast network of fabrication facilities Expanded capabilities and capacity: Adds significant engineering, fabrication, erection and industrial services capabilities and capacity in strategic locations Attractive long-term demand drivers: Positions IES to capitalize on demand across data centers, industrial reshoring, infrastructure investment, stadiums and arenas, and marquee commercial developments Experienced team and scalable systems: Brings an experienced management team and skilled craft workforce, supported by public-company-grade systems, processes and controls that enable disciplined execution and scalable growth “We’re excited to welcome DBM Global’s talented team to the IES family,” said Matt Simmes, President and Chief Executive Officer of IES. “This acquisition meaningfully broadens our product and service offerings and brings together highly complementary capabilities and teams. We look forward to investing in DBM Global’s people, facilities and equipment to enhance its operating capabilities and support the continued growth of its businesses and product lines as part of IES.” “DBM Global represents an attractive opportunity to acquire a premier business with leading market positions, durable demand drivers and strong cash flow generation,” said Jeff Gendell, Executive Chairman of IES. “We believe DBM Global will be an excellent addition to IES’s portfolio of businesses. We have also structured the transaction to maintain the strength and flexibility of our balance sheet, with the expectation that cash flow generated by IES and DBM Global will allow us to repay acquisition-related debt rapidly while preserving capacity to pursue additional acquisitions and investments.” “We see significant opportunity to leverage IES’s balance sheet strength to accelerate investment in our operations and to work alongside IES’s other operating segments to deliver a broader range of services to our customers, many of whom we have served for decades,” said Rustin Roach, President and Chief Executive Officer of DBM Global. “Together, we can build on the proud history of our businesses and the strength of our teams to create new opportunities for our employees and deliver even greater value to our customers.” Pursuant to the definitive agreement, IES will first acquire INNOVATE’s approximately 91.2% interest in DBM Global. Immediately following that closing, IES will acquire the remaining minority interests in DBM Global via a short form merger. Total consideration payable is approximately $685 million, comprised of approximately $545 million in cash and approximately $140 million in shares of IES common stock, with the cash consideration including a $35 million payment to INNOVATE in respect of the estimated cost to INNOVATE to participate in a joint election under Section 338(h)(10) of the Internal Revenue Code. About IES Holdings, Inc. IES designs and installs integrated electrical and technology systems and provides infrastructure solutions and services to a variety of end markets, including data centers, residential housing, and commercial and industrial facilities. Our more than 11,000 employees serve clients in the United States. For more information about IES, please visit www.ies-co.com . About DBM Global Inc. DBM Global is one of the largest independent structural steel fabrication and erection platforms in the United States, delivering vertically integrated engineering, fabrication, erection, industrial services and modular solutions for large-scale commercial, industrial, infrastructure and mission-critical projects. Operating through established brands including Schuff Steel, Banker Steel, GrayWolf, DBM Vircon and Aitken, DBM Global is headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. For more information, please visit www.dbmglobal.com . About INNOVATE Corp. INNOVATE Corp. title: Interview with the CEO: Billy Hult, Tradeweb
summary: BILLY HULT is Chief Executive Officer of Tradeweb Markets Inc. and a member of the board. Since joining Tradeweb in 2000, he has helped transform the company from a single-product platform for U.S. Treasuries into a leading global electronic marketplace across multiple asset classes. Mr. Hult became CEO in 2023 after serving 15 years as President — a tenure that included playing a key role in Tradeweb’s landmark IPO in 2019.
body_text: This article originally appeared in The Wall Street Transcript here . Billy Hult is Chief Executive Officer of Tradeweb Markets Inc. and a member of the board. Since joining Tradeweb in 2000, he has helped transform the company from a single-product platform for U.S. Treasuries into a leading global electronic marketplace across multiple asset classes. Mr. Hult became CEO in 2023 after serving 15 years as President — a tenure that included playing a key role in Tradeweb’s landmark IPO in 2019. As CEO, he has led Tradeweb through a period of substantial strategic expansion, broadening its product capabilities and geographic reach through the acquisitions of Yieldbroker, r8fin and ICD. An early champion of digital markets, Hult has driven Tradeweb's strategic investments and partnerships across blockchain, prediction markets, institutional crypto and digital assets, while also leading the company's AI deployment across execution, data, analytics and operations. Mr. Hult joined Tradeweb in 2000 after beginning his career at Société Générale. He holds a B.A. from Denison University. A fifth-generation New Yorker, he serves on the boards of the Tenement Museum and the Bridgehampton Chamber Music Festival. SECTOR — FINANCIAL SERVICES TWST: As I understand it, Tradeweb was founded in the late 1990s as an online trading network for U.S. Treasuries. What was the market like for this type of product then and what brought it about? Mr. Hult : I’ve been at the company since 2000, so I’m not a founder but I’ve had my 26-year run at the company. The original idea was that there were types of transactions that could be automated and done in a more efficient way over the internet. The concept of a salesperson standing on the trading floor and asking multiple dealers to provide liquidity to the client led someone to look at that transaction and say, “Isn’t there a better way to do this? Isn’t there a more valuable use of this person’s time than just being essentially a middleman on a standard transaction?” The idea, very early on, was how to think about electronic RFQs — requests for quotes — to allow big asset managers, hedge funds, and insurance companies to go to multiple dealers at once and ask them for a price. It made sense for us to start with government bonds because that was a big market and probably the most liquid market. But at the end of the day, the amazing thing is the basic business model of a client being able to look at a screen, see indicative prices in competition, and then be able to ask his or her counterparty for a price really works for global government bonds; and over time we extended this to mortgages, interest rate swaps, corporate bonds, and ETFs. So it’s become an amazing company that was really built off a very basic and simple idea. TWST: Since the internet became more mainstream for the general public in the 1990s, were there other platforms starting to serve markets besides the government side that Tradeweb played in? Mr. Hult : There was always Bloomberg looming out there at a minimum as a data company that was beginning to show prices for things. But we were really the first to pioneer around the trading or execution side of it in these markets. In an interesting but probably not surprising way, there was some resistance to it. Because from the trader’s perspective, as you can imagine, opaqueness was their friend. The more transparency there was, in some ways the more resistance we encountered. But the truth of the matter is, from the very, very beginning, the institutional client base loved it. Because it made their lives obviously more efficient, provided them transparency, and allowed them to get competitive prices in a real-time way they could not replicate over the phone. So there was momentum around it pretty early on. TWST: How has Tradeweb evolved since then? Mr. Hult : We continue to evolve, I think, from the concept of expansion. We started off in government bonds but, in a really good way, we didn’t just want to be a one-asset-class company. We wanted to be a global company that could take what we learned in Treasuries and extend that across marketplaces. We’ve been on a real journey of expansion from government bonds globally to liquid mortgages, to global interest rate swaps, ETFs, credit, emerging markets, and money market businesses like repurchase agreements. We’ve been on this continual journey of connecting the dots and getting into more and more of these marketplaces, providing the transparency and electronification that the client base really wants. I would say in a very interesting way, one thing that we’ve learned in this journey is that once markets begin to go electronic, that’s often the starting point for innovation. Even in our first market of government bonds, in a marketplace that is now mainstream electronic, there still is continual evolution around innovation and protocols. It’s been fun to take markets in a transparent way and then continue to innovate and make these markets more interesting. TWST: Are your clients mainly institutional investors or are you also focused on retail? Mr. Hult : We have a four-pronged and really amazing network. I think if I was going to go back in time, I would say one of the things the company did really well in the very beginning was to establish this very formidable and real network of clients. Think about our clients as institutional clients, so that hits the hedge funds, the insurance companies, asset managers, and central banks. Then think about the fact that we also have a wholesale business where banks connect with other banks to exchange liquidity in the wholesale markets. We also have a retail network, which encompasses the advisers, the RIAs of the world, around providing fixed income products to their clients. Then lastly, we have a really important network of corporates. We’re always really, really oriented toward our clients. I would say this: We are a technology company first and foremost, but we really try to be a technology company that lives and breathes in the financial services ecosystem. Staying close to this amazing network of clients has been, in some ways, our secret sauce from the very beginning. TWST: Looking back since your founding, what would you say have been the major milestones? Mr. Hult : A major milestone was executing those first electronic trades in government bonds way back in the day, where you’re dealing with professional clients and you’re actually able to accomplish something meaningfully different for your first clients. We never take our eyes off that early success that we had; it was really, really important. We wanted to remove siloes between markets, so the concept of expansion early on, making the kind of inroads that we made into the mortgage area, was a very big deal for us. And then the third thing I would say is the global interest rate swaps market and how we were able to navigate the regulatory landscape post-financial crisis and Dodd-Frank. Really establishing ourselves as the leading global derivatives platform is probably still one of the most important things that the company has done. Lastly, since becoming a public company in 2019, we’ve shown that we have the competitive chops to be quite successful in credit. Quite honestly, that may be the most important milestone so far. TWST: When did you do that? Mr. Hult : It was a little bit before our IPO in 2019, but our success and market share gains in credit really accelerated post-2020. We’re continually figuring out which are the protocols inside of the business that work well for the clients. And so it’s been fun. TWST: You’ve recently launched a dedicated Kalshi pricing page, which is interesting especially as predictive markets are all over the news right now. Why was this move important for Tradeweb? Mr. Hult : I think we have an orientation to be able to keep our eye on our day jobs, which is continuing to be leaders and expanding in these traditional financial markets that we’re known for. At the same time, I think we have a very strong perspective that the frontier markets in our space are, without question, important and becoming more important. We identified predictive markets as something that’s moving towards the realm of having institutional buy-in. We wanted to find the right partner, and we felt very strongly that Kalshi was the right partner for us. At a minimum, the table stakes around this is going to be that predictive markets data is ultimately going to be something that the professional marketplace will want. As I describe all of that to you, we also have a view that all Kalshi markets are not created equally. So the betting on Taylor Swift’s wedding date is not unbelievably interesting to us. But as there are financially oriented predictive markets that have a lot of ultimate liquidity in them and become a direct way to play event-driven outcomes, we want to be on the right side of that evolution and begin to integrate that liquidity into ours. It’s been a really interesting challenge for us to be the kind of company that’s going to be living and breathing in all of these traditional asset classes, these traditional marketplaces. But at the same time, we’re going to look to our right, and we’re going to see that there’s amazingly interesting innovations that continue to happen outside of traditional markets and more into the frontier space. We’re the right kind of company to partner with firms in that zone, too. TWST: Is there any hesitation given that predictive markets are being scrutinized by Congress now in the wake of some of the kinds of betting that have taken place? Mr. Hult : I don’t know if it’s hesitancy. I would say we are eyes wide open, very well aware all the time. We have a very strong reputation. I think we have a reputation of being a very credible marketplace, and there’s a lot of noise in the space. We know that, and we see that, and we see the headlines around all of that. That being said, I think it’s a smaller bet that we’re making. We still feel very strongly it’s an important bet, and sometimes you have to make the right bet on seeing that there will be changes in behavior and changes in outcome. We’re willing to do that. But as the expression goes, “Where do you go to get your reputation back? You don’t.” We take our reputation as an industry leader and a trusted platform in our network of clients extremely seriously. Small doses around this fits us really well, and we’re comfortable with it. We’re moving forward with a partnership there, and we think it’s going to work out. TWST: Let’s move on to talk about your growth strategy. I understand you’re in a quiet period now so we can’t discuss your Q2 results, but would you shed a little light on your M&A activity? You’ve done a number of deals in the last couple of years, most recently acquiring Institutional Cash Distribution — ICD — r8fin and Yieldbroker. What did these firms give Tradeweb that it didn’t already have, and are you looking for more? Mr. Hult : We’re always exceptionally oriented towards adding to this vaunted network that we have. All three of those deals added significant participants into our network. I feel very strongly that we have an excellent culture at Tradeweb, and so anytime we’re looking at an M&A deal, we want to make sure that the company is additive and fits into our culture in a way that works for us. Anytime that we can pick up — we have amazing developers and amazing technologists at the company — but anytime we feel like we can pick up a piece of technology faster than we can build, we’ll do that as well. We’ve largely gotten here as builders, not acquirers. A lot of the growth that we’ve had as a company has come through our own organic build and our own eyes around where we see opportunities for technology to be applied into these marketplaces. That being said, as a public company, we’re ambitious. Going forward, I think the general view is that we’re going to have opportunities to continue to make the right kind of consolidation plays inside of our business, and we’re going to be very, very open to that. The core belief is that the growth that we have, the credibility that we have as a company making the right kind of acquisitions, is only going to lead us towards more potential outcomes. But we’re going to be rigorous first and foremost around companies that fit our eye. TWST: What would that look like? Mr. Hult : It looks like continuing to add companies that grow our network and add into our network. TWST: What were you looking for when you found, for example, ICD? Mr. Hult : We were looking to add in this amazing client base of corporates into our world. We felt like that was a great business, and obviously we felt like the balance sheets of the corporate client base were going to continue to grow, and we wanted to be a part of that activity. At the same time, as you know very well, the integration of these kinds of deals is really important, so we also felt that there would be a significant appetite to introduce our marketplaces into these corporate clients, and we were going to be able to benefit from that as well. TWST: So ICD still exists, but Tradeweb sits inside it? Mr. Hult : Well it’s really become Tradeweb’s corporate client business. It works for us because we love their business model, and at the same time, we’re able to cross-sell our businesses, our marketplaces, into a client base that we hadn’t had before. We love Apple; they hadn’t been a meaningful client of ours until the ICD acquisition. So it’s kind of fun to continually fine-tune this big, giant network of clients that we have. TWST: Going forward, are you going to look for other deals where you can have that same kind of structure, or does that necessarily matter to you? Mr. Hult : Yeah, that structure matters to us. It’s always sort of the 1+1=3 dynamic that matters to us a lot. TWST: You’re scooping up a bigger client base by doing these acquisitions. Mr. Hult : For sure. You’re scooping up a bigger client base. We’re taking advantage of the liquidity and the leverage that we have inside of our own businesses. But we’re pretty open and creative to all different types of deals. TWST: Do you want to be approached with deals? Mr. Hult : We get approached all the time from amazingly interesting startup AI companies that come to us and say, “How we can help you get your development cycle going faster,” or things like that. We’ll be open-minded around that. We’re always looking for deals to be financially accretive to us, and it’s always going to be about the shareholder interest first and foremost. We are in a little bit of a sweet spot in our business because, as you know, debt markets continue to rise. There’s a tremendous amount of back-and-forth on where interest rates go from here. The legacy banks that have been a big part of our client base forever are doing exceptionally well in the businesses that we live in. You saw the earnings, they were just off the charts last week. At the same time, the non-bank liquidity providers, firms like Jane Street and Citadel Securities, are careening into our world with a lot of ambition and looking to pick up market share and make money in the businesses that we are in. That’s a really, really good environment for the marketplace and for companies like Tradeweb. So we feel like we’re in a strong position around our existing businesses. At the same time, being open-minded around change is fundamentally important. So yeah, we’re interested. We take a lot of phone calls, and we’ll have a lot of meetings around what’s out there, what aren’t we seeing, what does the crypto market look like in two years, will there be really interesting institutional behavior, will a client want to buy a government bond and exposure to gold and exposure to Bitcoin at the same time. We’re always very creative around what the world’s going to look like, or try to be. TWST: If you take a step back and look at the entire electronic trading sector, there’s been some volatility — high interest rates, possibility of future rate hikes, the war. How is the sector managing through this environment and is it preparing for a bumpy road ahead? Mr. Hult : What’s that expression — “Nobody knows anything”? It’s hard to predict what’s going to happen. What we would say very strongly is we really try to be laser-focused on things that we can control. We know we have a great business, we know we connect with our clients all the time, we know there’s a lot of wind at our sails around the continued electronification of the marketplaces that we live and breathe in, and we know that we’re the kind of company that likes to spend time with our clients on solving problems. I think if you focus on those things, you’re on the right path. And the other stuff, it’s not just noise, because obviously it affects us, stock price affects us, and all of those things. We live in the real world. But ultimately, we try to separate out the things that we can control versus the things that just exist out there in the marketplace that are beyond our control. I think when you think like that, you put yourself in a pretty good position. TWST: Would you elaborate a little more on the headwinds for the sector? Mr. Hult : I think the headwinds for the sector are around the unknown of what technology brings to the equation. What you’re getting more and more is, do marketplaces change, and do they change in such dramatic ways that I can’t tell who will be the winners and the losers five years from now or 10 years from now? I have a very, very strong belief that it’s the kind of companies that ultimately create and produce technology in the right way, that stay close to their clients around problem-solving, and that have the kind of reputation to continue to be the partner to build markets that will be the winners. It’s an unusual time. There’s no doubt about that. Four months ago, there were AI winners and losers, and then that shifted a few months later, and then that will shift again a few months later. We knew what perpetual future contracts were nine months ago, but we didn’t know that they would become in the mainstream of conversation. It just shows you how quickly the world changes. But you focus on what you can control. From my perspective, when I think about the business that we have, I start with scale. We were over $2 billion in revenue last year, and we’re having a very good year this year. So the scale is real. And then you go into growth, so we’ve had significant years in a row with double-digit revenue growth. Then we’ve had +50% margins and the ability to expand our margins as a company as we’ve created scale and created growth. When you take those three things together — scale, growth and profitability — I feel like we’re in a little bit of rarefied air as a company that does all three. That makes me confident that we’re going to be the kind of company that navigates change really well. That being said, you never take anything for granted. So the concept of not taking your eye off the ball and maintaining an intensity around change, I think, is fundamentally important. TWST: How does Tradeweb differentiate itself among its peers? Mr. Hult : Meet the management team. Spend time with management teams. I think the more investors get to know management teams, I think that’s a really good starting point. I think past records matter, but really at the end of the day, when you close your eyes and imagine what the world’s going to look like, imagine what kind of companies are going to navigate the future the best. I feel like that’s going to be a combination of companies that really understand the markets that they’re in, companies that really understand what their clients want, and ultimately that multi-asset-class marketplace that has the kind of leverage around deploying technology from one market to another, I think, is a really, really important premise around continued growth going forward. TWST: What’s important for people to know about your company. Mr. Hult : I would say this: It’s an amazing privilege to be the CEO of a public company. I take it very, very seriously. I’ve been at the company for, as I mentioned, 26 years, so a lot of pride of authorship around that. We have a great management team, we work together really well, so it’s certainly way beyond and way past me. A technology company that lives and breathes as a public market, not always easy. So I’ll be very, very blunt with you about that, because sometimes change can occur at different rates than you expect. When you’re a public company, as you know very well, you have public shareholders, and they expect results sometimes within parameters, and it doesn’t always happen that way. But from my perspective, one of the things that I do and the team does really well is stay patient, constantly making the kind of investments for medium- and longer-term change. I think that’s a really, really important ethos as we’re navigating this next leg of growth. TWST: Lastly, if you had to name just one major thing you have in store for the future, what would it be? Mr. Hult : I think navigating AI is, without question, one of the most important things for a company, including ours. One of the most important things that we will think about is really how our clients use AI and machine learning to continue to find best prices in the market. That’s going to hold true for traditional markets and frontier markets. We have exceptional data and the exceptional ability to produce technology that works for our clients, and our goal will be to have a leadership role around AI in terms of our clients’ search for best price and liquidity in these marketplaces. The great news is our clients are continuing to get more and more sophisticated, and they look to us as the problem solver for sophisticated problems, and that’s a great place to be. TWST: Thank you.

title: My Datsun’s Wiring Harness Crumbled to Dust, with No Factory Replacement Available
summary: In his novel The Sun Also Rises, Ernest Hemingway describes the path to bankruptcy as unfolding “gradually, then suddenly.” That same timeline could easily be applied to the trajectory that saw me needing to replace the entire wiring harness in my 1978 Datsun 280Z this summer.
